explanation: Recursively obtain each subtree’s list head and tail, then connect those lists through the original root. Original nodes become the doubly linked list and the head’s previous link is null.
timeComplexity: O(n): recursive calls visit each original node once and perform constant link work.
spaceComplexity: O(h) recursion frames, where h is the original tree height; nodes are reused, so a skew tree may require O(n) auxiliary stack.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/bst_to_sorted_list.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Inductively each recursive result is a sorted doubly linked list with correct head and tail. Link the left tail to the root and the root to the right head; BST inorder order makes the concatenation sorted. Missing children contribute null endpoints, so the returned head has no predecessor and the tail has no successor.
walkthrough: For tree [5,2,8,1,3], recursion converts the left subtree into 1↔2↔3 and the right subtree into the singleton 8. Joining left tail 3 to root 5 and root 5 to right head 8 gives the same original nodes in order [1,2,3,5,8].
edgeCases: A singleton becomes a list with both links null.
Both child conversions finish before root links become list links.
